pr_body:
Fixes #92570

A watcher responsible for restarting stuck range feeds may incorrectly cancel rangefeed if the downstream event consumer is slow.

Release note (bug fix): Fix incorrect cancellation logic when attempting to detect stuck range feeds.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/92582)

> ely approving once addressed.

> We should also have a test, either for the DistSender or as a CDC roachtest

Added canceller test.

issue_context.title: kvcoord: `stuckRangeFeedCanceler` can fire during event processing
issue_context.body:
In #86820, we added `stuckRangeFeedCanceler` which will restart stuck rangefeeds after a period of inactivity. This was meant as a mitigation for #86818. However, it can wrongfully fire if client-side event processing is slow as well (notably if the event sink is slow), and in this case it will not return `errRestartStuckRange` which is automatically retried by the DistSender, but instead a bare context cancellation error which is propagated back up to the client, causing the entire changefeed to restart.

The watcher is meant to fire here:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/98ab46127ea09c11c9c50d5cb7319cae421d24dd/pkg/kv/kvclient/kvcoord/dist_sender_rangefeed.go#L643-L654

However, the ping registers a `time.AfterFunc` hook which cancels the rangefeed context here:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2675c7c0481bb33eb9f43f1c2b52c152fca3ae2d/pkg/kv/kvclient/kvcoord/dist_sender_rangefeed_canceler.go#L88-L94

This can fire during event processing here:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/98ab46127ea09c11c9c50d5cb7319cae421d24dd/pkg/kv/kvclient/kvcoord/dist_sender_rangefeed.go#L686-L692

In which case it returns the bare `ctx.Err()` rather than `errRestartStuckRange`. It should only apply to the `Recv()` call and similar upstream activity, not downstream activity.

Jira issue: CRDB-21873

review_comments: We should add another test that makes sure it won't fire when the processing time between `do()` calls is much greater than the threshold (e.g. 2x).
We should document the state machine and possible transitions here.

We'll no longer handle any hangs between here and `Recv()`. Is that problematic? It's probably ok, since the hangs we have seen have all been in `Recv()`, and trying to be clever here could lead to unintended issues.
We'll need to update the comments that refer to `ping()` and the overall logic flow.
We're adding in three atomic operations in the hot path here. Do we need to benchmark the overhead of these, or is it likely negligible once we factor in IO and such?
